topic: A person learns their childhood best friend doesn't remember them
text: I can't help but fumble with the edges of my shirt as I replay the conversation, the one where the connection I thought was unbreakable turned out to be fragile, almost nonexistent. I asked, simple question, hoping for a flood of memories, shared secrets, inside jokes. Instead, there was a pause, long and heavy. "I'm sorry," they said, and I could almost see them shrug, "I don't remember." The words hung there, between us, a stark reminder of how time erodes even the most cherished parts of us. I nodded, even though they couldn’t see, and changed the subject, my voice a bit too high, a bit too eager.
